== Biography ==
== Research Notes ==
=== Children and the Miami Valley account ===

The memoir of [[Glasgow-2043|Samuel Steele Glasgow]] identifies his father [[Glasgow-875|William B. Glasgow]] and names the following family. [[Glasgow-1625|Robert Anderson]]’s 1880 county biography provides the Joseph/Nancy parent identification; the memoir itself leaves the grandfather unnamed. Six combined father identifications are assessed individually below. <ref name="Miami1919">John C. Hover et al., eds., ''Memoirs of the Miami Valley'' (Robert O. Law Company, 1919–1920), “S. S. Glasgow,” printed pp. 257–258; [https://digital.cincinnatilibrary.org/iiif/2/p16998coll15:18001/full/full/0/default.jpg original p. 257] and [https://digital.cincinnatilibrary.org/iiif/2/p16998coll15:18002/full/full/0/default.jpg original p. 258], Cincinnati & Hamilton County Public Library Digital Library; images inspected 22 October 2026. Published family biography, not a civil or parish register.</ref>

The Scottish immigrant-grandfather tradition conflicts with Joseph’s Virginia birth and may telescope generations. Eliza’s recorded 1831 birth and Campbell parentage show that the list may mix maternal half-siblings. No mother or earlier ancestor is inferred from that preamble. The two publications may share family information; they are not assumed independent.


FAG reports his death in 1820 in  Ohio.
=== Parentage ===

David Faris's dedicated genealogy of [[Glasgow-12|Robert Glasgow]] and [[Barclay-56|Rosanna Barclay]] identifies '''Joseph Glasgow''' among their ten children. This family reconstruction agrees with the migration and sibling evidence summarized on Robert's profile, so both parent relationships are treated as confident.

=== Individual father review, 22 October 2026 ===

The existing father [[Glasgow-12]] is assessed at 93% (proved). The dedicated Faris genealogy, as explicitly summarized in the held biography, identifies Joseph among Robert and Rosanna’s children. Joseph’s 1780 Virginia birth fits the specific Robert household and subsequent Adams County family.

Compiled-family attribution93%, not an inference from surname or DNA. The underlying book page and parental record are uninspected in this review.

Next useful test: Check Joseph’s chapter and its underlying family record alongside the sibling entries.

Source basis already held: [https://search.worldcat.org/title/22731567 David Faris, The Glasgow Family of Adams County, Ohio (1990); specific retained family statements and page citations identified in each reviewed pair]. No new original inspected; no new father attached.
